findings.title: RemoteSession can exfiltrate an arbitrary referenced Secret to a repository host
findings.what: Both GitCredentialRef and Repo come from the RemoteSession spec. The operator mounts the named Secret, reads its token, embeds it in a URL derived from Repo, and runs git clone. A caller permitted to create or update RemoteSession objects can therefore select another same-namespace Secret and an attacker-controlled HTTPS host, causing the operator-created pod to disclose that token during clone authentication.
findings.fix: Authorize GitCredentialRef against an operator-managed allowlist or dedicated credential binding, and validate Repo before mounting or reading the token so credentialed clones are limited to explicitly trusted HTTPS hosts. Prefer a credential helper that supplies credentials only after an exact host match instead of embedding the token in the URL.
findings.acceptance: A test constructs a RemoteSession with GitCredentialRef naming an unauthorized Secret and Repo set to an untrusted HTTPS host; reconciliation must reject it or build no pod containing that Secret. A second test proves an approved secret/host binding still clones without placing the token in the persisted remote URL.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 167-175 mount the CR-selected Secret and lines 182-196 send its token through the CR-selected repository URL. Environment-variable quoting prevents shell injection but does not prevent credential disclosure to the selected network host.

findings.title: PoolHealthy reports claimed pods as warm
findings.what: The controller computes warm by excluding pods labeled claimed=true and persists that value in Status.WarmReady, but the PoolHealthy message uses len(running). Consequently, with one claimed running pod and poolSize=1, WarmReady is 0 while the condition claims "1/1 warm" and PoolHealthy=True. The status evidence is internally contradictory and can falsely report pool readiness.
findings.fix: Build the condition message from warm, and set PoolHealthy=True only when the required warm capacity is actually present; account explicitly for newly created pods if Pending is intended to count as warm capacity.
findings.acceptance: A reconciliation test with one claimed Running pod and poolSize=1 asserts WarmReady=0 and verifies that PoolHealthy does not report "1/1 warm" or PoolReady until an unclaimed replacement is observed in the pod list.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-derived the counters: running includes claimed Running/Pending pods at lines 69-74, warm excludes them, Status.WarmReady uses warm at line 173, but the condition claim uses len(running) at line 224. The contradiction is directly reproducible without relying on external documentation.
